requirement: Implement StreamSafeDataProcessor with max_depth validation to prevent JSON recursion errors, chunk-based CSV streaming without full in-memory read, trailing batch preservation, and safe column summaries.
skeleton: StreamSafeDataProcessor class with safe_parse_json, stream_csv_records, and compute_column_summary.
caption: A standard-library data processor with three methods over csv, io, and json. safe_parse_json scans the raw JSON string character by character before parsing, incrementing a depth counter on every opening brace or bracket and decrementing on every closing one with a floor of zero, and raises ValueError with a message naming the limit as soon as the depth exceeds max_depth, which defaults to 20, so a deeply nested document is rejected at the guard rather than reaching json.loads and hitting the interpreter's recursion limit; a document within the limit is returned from json.loads. stream_csv_records raises ValueError for a batch_size at or below zero, wraps the file object in csv.DictReader, and iterates row by row, copying each row to a plain dict and yielding a batch as soon as it reaches batch_size, so only one batch is ever held in memory and the first batch is available after reading a handful of lines; after the loop it yields the remaining partial batch when it is non-empty, so five rows at a batch size of two produce batches of two, two, and one. compute_column_summary reads the named column through csv.DictReader, skipping missing and blank cells and cells whose float conversion raises ValueError, and tracks count, sum, running minimum, and running maximum in a single pass. When no numeric cell was seen it returns all five keys as 0.0 instead of calling min or max on nothing; otherwise it returns count, sum, mean, min, and max as floats.

plan.intent: Parse JSON and CSV input without unbounded recursion or memory
constraints: Nesting deeper than the limit raises ValueError before json.loads runs
CSV rows are yielded in batches as they are read, with the trailing partial batch last
A batch size of zero or less raises ValueError
A column summary skips blank and non-numeric cells in one pass
A column without numeric cells reports zeros instead of failing

rationale.teaches: Streaming-safe data handling: a depth pre-scan before json.loads with a sane default, batch-wise CSV iteration that never materializes the file, the trailing partial batch emitted, and an empty-column summary that returns zeros.
rationale.why: A generator that reads the whole file into a list produces identical batches and only differs in memory. The fixture measures peak memory and feeds deeply nested JSON, which is where these misses separate from gold.

ops.docstring: Parse JSON and stream CSV without unbounded recursion or memory.

candidates.why_wrong: The depth pre-scan is gone, so deeply nested JSON reaches json.loads and blows the recursion limit instead of raising ValueError.
The CSV is read fully into a list before batching, so a large file consumes memory proportional to its size.
max_depth defaults to 10000, so the depth guard never fires before Python's own recursion limit does.
The trailing partial batch is never yielded, so rows past the last full batch are silently dropped.
The empty-column guard is removed, so summarizing an empty column raises on min and max.
